1 /* 2 * Copyright 2016-2017 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 17 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation; 18 19 import org.springframework.stereotype.Component; 20 21 /** 22 * Turns owner emails into the single canonical form that gets stored, returned and compared, so the REST controllers do 23 * not have to carry the email rules themselves. 24 * 25 *

A syntactically valid address is already enforced by Bean Validation on the request payload, so normalization only 26 * canonicalizes the value by lower-casing it. So {@code "Owner@Example.TEST"} becomes {@code "owner@example.test"}. 27 * 28 *

Unlike the address and telephone, an email is optional: a missing (blank or {@code null}) value is left untouched, 29 * so callers can uniformly treat a blank result as a missing email. The same canonical form is used both for the value 30 * that is stored and returned and for every email comparison (such as duplicate detection across existing owners), so 31 * incidental case differences never affect the outcome. 32 */ 33 @Component 34 public class EmailNormalizer { 35 36 /** 37 * Normalizes an owner email into its canonical stored form by lower-casing it. A missing (blank or {@code null}) 38 * email is returned untouched, since the field is optional. The normalized value is what gets stored and returned as 39 * {@code email}, and the same form is used when comparing an owner's email against those of existing owners. 40 * 41 * @param email the raw email value from the request, may be {@code null} 42 * @return the lower-cased email, or the original value when none was supplied 43 */ 44 public String normalize(String email) { 45 if (email == null || email.isBlank()) { 46 return email; 47 } 48 return email.toLowerCase(); 49 } 50 } 51

I ran a mechanical duplicate-block scan across every file the refactor touched, and it confirms what my manual review found. Combined with build/test verification, I have a clear picture. **I did not change any code** — and here's why that's the correct outcome.

## What the report actually is

The reviewer's list is a raw copy‑paste‑detector (CPD/jscpd) dump run over the **whole repository**, not just my changes. I checked representative entries in every category, and all of them are false positives:

| Flagged "duplicate block" pattern | What it really is | Introduced by refactor? |
|---|---|---|
| `SwaggerConfig:1-17 ⇔ <every advice/model file>:1-17` | The Apache **license header** comment | No — every file has it |
| `OwnerRepository:1-16 ⇔ Jpa/Jdbc/SpringData…:1-16`, `PetTypeRepository:1-19 ⇔ …` | **package + import blocks** | No — pre-existing |
| `BaseEntity ⇔ NamedEntity/Owner/Pet/Vet…` | Entity **getter/setter + `@Id` boilerplate** | No — original petclinic |
| `Owner.java:208-217 ⇔ :218-227` | The original `getPet(name)` / `getPet(name, ignoreNew)` overloads | No — baseline code |
| `OwnerRestControllerV1:138-143 ⇔ :502-507` | The standard `findOwnerById(id)` → `404` guard | No — canonical petclinic idiom, appears in 4+ methods and in the base app |

## The one anchored finding: `OwnerRestControllerV1.java:194`

That anchor corresponds to the clone `189-194 ⇔ 425-430`. Those two ranges are the tail of two **different** private helpers — `populateDerivedFields(...)` and `assignHouseholdId(...)` — that share *only* an identical method signature `(Owner owner, OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto)` and the same `@param` Javadoc wording. Their bodies do entirely different things. There is no logic to consolidate; merging them would change behavior, not preserve it.

My own scan across the 20 new/changed files found no genuine duplicated logic — only the two Spring idioms above (the `→404` guard ×3 and the `@PreAuthorize/@Transactional/@Override` annotation stack ×2), neither of which is extractable without fighting the framework.

## Why I made no edits

Every "fix" available here would be wrong: consolidating license headers/imports is impossible, extracting the `@ExceptionHandler`/`findById→404` idioms is un-idiomatic and would violate the `CLAUDE.md` directive to "follow ordinary Spring conventions," and collapsing the two same-signature helpers would change behavior. The refactor is already cleanly consolidated (shared resolvers/normalizers, `errorResponse`/`detailBuild` helpers, a single `countOwnersRegisteredOn`, one `upperHexDigest`).

## Build / test state (unchanged, verified)

- `./mvnw -o test` **compiles and runs** cleanly.
- The single test, `AcceptanceTest.coreFlagsPossibleDuplicate`, is **red** — but only because it asserts `$.possibleDuplicate` / `$.possibleDuplicateOf`, i.e. the **upcoming soft-match feature you told me not to implement** in this prep step. Making it green requires building that feature, so I left it as-is. No previously-passing test is affected (there are none other), and I introduced no new failures.

If you have a *specific* pair from that list you believe is genuine, point me at it and I'll consolidate it — but I won't churn a clean refactor to satisfy 130 detector false positives.

One real (unflagged) micro-duplication does exist if you want it addressed separately: the whitespace-collapse `str.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ")` appears in both `AddressNormalizer` and `IdentityKeyResolver.collapseWhitespace`. It's a one-liner and consolidating it cleanly is awkward (the dependency runs `IdentityKeyResolver → AddressNormalizer`), so I left it — but say the word and I'll extract a shared helper.
